newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: VILNIUS BANK LEADS AS SHARES RISE.
newsitem.headline: VILNIUS BANK LEADS AS SHARES RISE.

text.p: Market leader Vilnius Bank, which saw its 1996 net profit soar, propelled Lithuania's shares up on Monday, dealers said.
Overall central market volume in equities was 1.14 million litas and the Litin A index of leading shares rose by 14.15 points to 2,604.64.

Vilnius Bank was one of the session's biggest blue chip gainers, with preference shares rising by 9.79 percent to 1,570 litas in trade worth 62,800 litas. Its ordinary shares climbed 2.73 percent to 259.90 litas on turnover of 18,200 litas.
The bank earlier on Monday announced that its 1996 profit climbed steeply to 24.4 million litas versus 2.9 million litas the previous year.
Dealers were divided over what impact the results would have on its share price in the coming weeks.
"It will look like a good buy right now," said one dealer.
But other dealers said the results were what the market had anticipated and so the effect would be minimal.
"The results are what the market expected, so I don't think they will move the share price very much," said Tomas Andrejauskas of brokerage firm Suprema.
Naftos terminalas also gained substantially, rising by 9.82 percent to 120.80 litas in light trade of 2,899 litas.
Snaige refrigerator producer leapt by 9.52 percent to 11.50 litas in trade worth over 207,000 litas.
Dealers say that the factory is relatively attractive as it agressively seeks new markets in the west.
The session's losers included Birzai Milk, which slipped to 10.10 litas from 11.00 litas in trade worth just over 8,000 litas.
Block trades worth over 318,000 litas were also made.
The secondary T-bill market remained in the doldrums, turing over almost 500,000 litas.
Low yields have dampened investor interest but analysts anticipate that the central bank's decision to begin repo auctions next month will rekindle activity in the market.
